apps.localizedDescription: Luma reads a WHOOP strap you own directly over Bluetooth and turns it into recovery, sleep and strain each morning, GPS running with splits and spoken cues, HYROX race mode and readiness, a food and supplement log, and a coach. Your data stays on the phone; the coach runs on your own Anthropic key and reads only what you let it. A personal, non-commercial build on open-source foundations, credited in the app's About screen; not affiliated with WHOOP or HYROX.

versions.localizedDescription: Build 22. Two experiments: counting from wrist motion, and a trace from the clasp. Both are off until you switch them on, on the Strap screen. Neither has been tried on a strap yet. Counting from motion: with "Record motion with sessions" and "Count from motion" both on, Luma counts from the movement of your wrist after a session: steps a minute in a run, strokes on the SkiErg and rower, reps at a station. A session with parts (a simulation, intervals, a led workout) is counted part by part. A session with none, such as a class recorded as one piece, is split into runs, work and rest. The counts show on the session's screen and under each recording on the Strap screen, and change nothing in the session itself. It is an estimate, checked so far only against made-up movement. Enter your own number beside a count and Luma shows how far off it has been. Walking about between sets is counted with them. Trace from the clasp (WHOOP MG only): holding the clasp with your other hand for about 40 seconds gives a trace of your heartbeat. Luma counts its beats for a heart rate, and shows how much the time between beats varied. It is a trial: the strap may not answer on this software, and the screen says what the strap answered either way. The trace is a recording, not a check of your heart. Luma does not look for rhythm problems and shows nothing the strap's own software concluded. See a doctor about any worry.
